title: Lattice symmetry breaking and strain control of single-$\mathbf{q}$ magnetism in Na$_3$Co$_2$SbO$_6$
authors: Yuchen Gu, Wu Xie, Xintong Li, Junhong Liu, Xianghong Jin, Dmitry Khalyavin, Fabio Orlandi, Pascal Manuel, Ping Miao, Yuan Li
abstract: Distinguishing single-$\mathbf{q}$ from multi-$\mathbf{q}$ magnetism constrains microscopic spin Hamiltonians. Here we determine the ground state of the candidate Kitaev magnet Na$_3$Co$_2$SbO$_6$ through its coupling to the lattice. High-resolution neutron diffraction reveals a spontaneous monoclinic-to-triclinic distortion at the magnetic transition, in contrast to the absence of detectable lattice-symmetry breaking in triple-$\mathbf{q}$ Na$_2$Co$_2$TeO$_6$. Together with strain-selective magnetic responses, this identifies single-$\mathbf{q}$ order in Na$_3$Co$_2$SbO$_6$ over the proposed symmetry-preserving double-$\mathbf{q}$ state. Uniaxial compression along a low-symmetry in-plane direction achieves the domain selection that magnetic-field training could not, revealing the intrinsic field-induced phase boundaries of the dominant domain. These results establish strain as a symmetry-conjugate field for magnetic domains and highlight magnetoelastic coupling as a route to diagnose, manipulate, and potentially tune magnetic states.
summary: This work investigates the magnetic ordering in $	ext{Na}_3	ext{Co}_2	ext{SbO}_6$ by linking magnetic structure to lattice symmetry. Using neutron diffraction and controlled uniaxial strain, the authors confirm single-$\mathbf{q}$ magnetism via lattice distortion and demonstrate that strain can deterministically select magnetic domains. This establishes magnetoelastic coupling as a key tool for diagnosing and tuning quantum magnetic states.
main_problem: The study aims to distinguish between single-$\mathbf{q}$ and multi-$\mathbf{q}$ magnetic ordering in the Kitaev magnet $	ext{Na}_3	ext{Co}_2	ext{SbO}_6$ by coupling the magnetic state to the lattice symmetry.
main_result: Neutron diffraction reveals a spontaneous lattice distortion in $	ext{Na}_3	ext{Co}_2	ext{SbO}_6$ consistent with single-$\mathbf{q}$ order, while strain control was shown to select magnetic domains, establishing magnetoelastic coupling as a diagnostic tool.
method: The research combines high-resolution neutron diffraction measurements to probe lattice symmetry breaking with controlled uniaxial strain application to manipulate magnetic domains.
model_or_system: The system is the honeycomb cobaltate $	ext{Na}_3	ext{Co}_2	ext{SbO}_6$, analyzed using a bond-equivalent nearest-neighbor $J-K-\Gamma-\Gamma'$ model derived from the Kitaev model framework.
key_observables: Lattice symmetry breaking (monoclinic-to-triclinic distortion), splitting of nuclear reflections, domain selection via strain, and magnetic susceptibility anisotropy.
important_parameters: Magnetic transition temperature ($T_N$), strain magnitude ($\epsilon_{ab}$), and the sign/magnitude of the effective Kitaev interaction ($K_{	ext{eff}}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the lattice distortion is directly coupled to the magnetic order parameter, and that strain can induce domain selection by coupling to the magnetic shear.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the splitting of diffraction reflections confirming symmetry breaking in $	ext{NCSO}$ versus the lack thereof in $	ext{NCTO}$, and show how strain alters the angular dependence of magnetic susceptibility, revealing domain selection.
paper_structure: The paper first uses diffraction to distinguish single-$\mathbf{q}$ from multi-$\mathbf{q}$ order. It then applies strain to study domain selection, revealing intrinsic phase boundaries. Finally, theoretical modeling compares the stability of different spin patterns (zigzag vs. UUD) under these constraints.
why_interesting: The explicit coupling between lattice strain and magnetic domain selection provides a powerful, experimentally verifiable method to probe the underlying symmetry constraints of complex magnetic Hamiltonians, which is highly relevant for understanding emergent quantum phases.
